column2: req_desc

Pinned stage.
On `/showroom` a single fixed stage holds the procedurally built motorcycle while scrolling drives its published progress from 0 to 1.

Part seating.
The seven part groups seat in the published order, and each group's offset moves monotonically with progress in both scroll directions.

Showroom URL state.
The URL holds the model, hub, finish, chapter, part and progress, so a reload, a resize, opening or closing `Menu` or a shared link opened signed out keeps the same pose, as qualified in Interactions.

Scroll input.
Wheel input is damped over native scroll and settles within the published limit, chapter statements shift at the published rate, and touch uses native scroll with no damping.

Chapters toolbar.
The toolbar `Chapters` jumps to each of the seven chapters by pointer, touch and keyboard, with one tab stop and arrow-key movement.

Parts list.
Selecting a part in listbox `Parts` by pointer, keyboard or touch moves the camera to it and lifts it, and the selection survives a reload, Back, a live event and a shared link, as qualified in Interactions.

Published choreography.
Every animated step runs at its published duration and is reported in the probe, and no step ever runs at 0 ms.

Key-On reading.
Once the cluster has seated, the needle, display, tank paint and tell-tale repaint from one server reading, the needle clamps at the published hours, and canvas pixels agree with the probe at the tank, tell-tale, needle tip and display.

Newest reading wins.
The scene draws only the newest server sequence for the current selection, as qualified in Business rules, and a local action never changes a drawn count.

Showroom probe.
`window.__showroom.snapshot()` returns every published field, and the canvas stays readable for pixel checks.

Live feed.
`GET /api/live/now` and the stream `GET /api/live` publish a per-hub sequence that reaches open screens within the limit stated in API.

Context loss and return.
When the browser loses the WebGL context the showroom pauses, keeps the rider's place and refuses scene input while purchases keep working, and it returns to the same place with the newest reading and the model and finish chosen while paused, every time.

No-WebGL showroom.
When no WebGL context can be created, a side elevation per chapter, present in the raw server HTML, shows the same live values and updates in place, including on a model change and with a wrong device clock.

Reduced-motion showroom.
With the reduced-motion setting on, the Chapters toolbar steps through seven posed stills with the published dissolve, live values, the tell-tale, URL state and purchase functions all stay the same, and a change of the setting on an open page applies with no reload and keeps pose and selection.

On-road quote.
The server quotes the on-road price for the chosen model and hub city from the published make-up, and the newest choice wins over any slower reply.

Price steps.
An on-road quote moves to a new price step at midnight IST on its effective date without a reload, while an existing lock keeps the step it was issued on.

Amount display.
Amounts are integer paise shown with Indian digit grouping in every browser locale, no amount appears before its data arrives, and after a failed read the last amount is labelled with its as-of time until the first good reading clears it in place.

Hub stock reading.
Units left come from the hub's on-hand count minus its active holds, stale readings are labelled as Services describes, and every surface shows the same count.

Lock claim.
`POST /api/locks` holds a unit for a rider only once the ledger gate and Postgres have both committed, with one winner for the last unit and one ledger member for a repeated submit.

Last unit floor check.
A claim that takes units left to 0 stays requested and counts as a hold until the hub host confirms or refuses it, with its amounts fixed at acceptance, as qualified in Business rules.

Lock dialog.
Dialog `Confirm your lock` shows the server's amounts and expiry, traps focus, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener.

Lock expiry.
A lock ends at the instant Business rules compute on the app clock, as in the published expiry table, whatever the browser's clock says.

Lock card and release.
The Garage lock band survives refresh and live updates, flips in place at the server's expiry, ticks its hours at each whole IST hour and ends the lock on release only once the hold ledger confirms removal.

Session ending.
A session ends on the app clock, and any open screen then announces it once and offers an in-place sign-in that keeps form values, URL and step.

Price sheet.
A confirmed lock renders to a stored PDF with the locked amounts, hub and either its IST expiry or, on a delivery-set lock, its delivery day, is never ready before a successful render, and can be retried after a failed one.

Test-ride slots.
Grid `Test-ride slots` lists the published slot starts on IST dates with server-given Today and Tomorrow labels, in any browser zone and by keyboard, and a cell disables in place at its cut-off.

Ride claim.
`POST /api/rides` gives one winner for a slot through its ledger key and at most one active ride per rider per model.

Licence check.
A ride requires an MCWG licence that is valid on the ride's IST date, and this is checked with the published boundary.

Ride move and cancel.
Moving and cancelling a ride work only before the published cut-off, a move swaps its ledger keys, and a refusal at the exact cut-off shows no false success.

Hub day sheet.
A hub host sees only their own hub's table `Day sheet` on IST dates, and it changes in place with exactly the published row fields and licence numbers cut to the last 4 characters.

Ride and handover marks.
Only the hub host marks a ride ridden or a no-show at or after its start, and a handover delivered on or after its delivery day, with one outcome when two hosts mark one record.

Delivery-day rules.
Grid `Delivery days` offers days inside the published window, closes each day in place at the published time and shows server-given capacity.

Delivery-day claim.
`POST /api/locks/{id}/delivery` gives exactly one winner for the last place on a day, including Dhanteras, and one honest refusal to each other claimant.

Reminder opt-in.
`Turn on reminders` shows reminders as on only after ntfy accepts the confirmation notice, and a failure does not stick.

Phone notices.
Opted-in riders get each lock-ending, ride and delivery-place notice once at its published time, as qualified in Business rules, with no licence number or full mobile number in it.

Accounts.
Riders create accounts and riders and hub hosts sign in from an in-place dialog, with sessions held in a cookie the browser's scripts cannot read.

Error precedence.
Every API error follows one precedence and one body shape, using only the published codes and answering each row of the worked matrix in API exactly, malformed bodies included.

Server boundaries.
A rider reads only their own records, a host only their own hub, every reply belongs only to its caller, and the server never accepts prices, expiry times, states or unit counts from a client.

Status region.
One polite status region named `Showroom status` announces the exact published strings on every screen, each transition once.

Layout and touch.
No route overflows sideways at 375, 768 or 1280 px wide, phone touch targets are at least 44 px, focus is always visible as the published ring, and the closed parts sheet and closed `Menu` links are out of the tab order.

Provider recovery.
The app starts with any provider down, shows honest paused screens during an outage and recovers without a restart once the provider returns.

First screen.
The first screen shows the cropped word MALHAR, the sentence, the action and the top bar at the published values, with no machine visible until the first scroll.

Working screens.
Working screens carry the statement headings, banded timetable, large numerals, stacked Garage bands, square corners and light outage field at the published values.

Machine drawing.
The motorcycle is drawn procedurally with the published proportions, axes, sides and lean, and shows them in pixels, camera positions and `snapshot.geometry`.

Source discipline.
Source holds money as integers, takes the time, errors and easing from one place each, bundles its fonts and contains no literal seed passwords or model assets.

Server instants.
A hub's sequence also rises at each slot's cut-off, each slot's start and each lock expiry there, so open screens repaint within the limit stated in API, as in the worked Pune example in Business rules.

Rider stream.
A signed-in rider's stream carries an event for any change to their records at any hub and at every whole IST hour while they hold a lock, and the page re-opens the stream after any change of identity so the reading belongs to the current caller.

Stream recovery.
When the stream ends or answers with a failure the page keeps re-opening it and keeps reading in the meantime, within the limits stated in API, with no reload.

Lock dialog over time.
An open `Confirm your lock` repaints amounts and expiry in place, disables and re-enables `Confirm lock` on stock and hub changes, and a price that moved gets 409 `price_moved` with no lock and no ledger member.

Requested lock survives reload.
A requested lock shows no amounts as locked and no release on any load, announces that it is being checked, and announces its exact result on any open screen when the hub host settles it.

Hub withdrawal.
A hub host's withdrawal of a locked or delivery-set lock makes it withdrawn, which in one transition stops the hold, lowers on-hand, frees the delivery place, promotes the next rider in line, removes the handover row, cancels the notice, drops the needle and announces it.

Session over dialogs and a different rider.
Dialog `Sign in` opens over any open dialog and resumes it with re-read amounts and focus restored, and if a different account signs in the chosen cell and URL stay, licence fields clear and all rider data is replaced.

Re-reads keep the rider's place.
A live re-read keeps focus, roving tabindex, chosen cell, typed text with its caret, scroll position, selected part and any open dialog by updating the existing elements, as qualified in Interactions.

Host actions from the server.
Each day-sheet row carries server-made actions, mark buttons exist only for those actions and appear in place at the instant, and the sheet follows today across midnight IST unless another date is chosen.

Any process or browser zone.
Ride days, slots, delivery days, delivery dates and the day sheet are identical whatever zone the server process or browser runs in, including zones whose clocks change on 1 November 2026.

Family reader.
A signed-out reader of a shared URL gets the same pose with no sign-in prompt on phone, under reduced motion and with a wrong device clock, sees price and stock change in place, and receives exactly the published public fields.

Exact easing and measured steps.
Every page and scene animation uses the one published easing, reported as that exact text, and each step's measured time and sampled needle match their published duration and curve.

Amount and stale-hub edges.
`Lock this price` stays disabled until a current reading is drawn, a changed hub never shows the previous city's amount, a stale hub does not make the quote stale, and Garage amounts come only from the lock.

Provider edges.
Parallel presses across copies make one render and one confirmation notice, a 200 reply that is not a complete PDF is a failure, a rider's name holding markup prints as literal text, the download link appears in other open tabs, and a sheet made after a price step keeps the lock's amounts.

Outage per hub.
Staleness from a count or damaged key belongs to one hub and each transition announces once, a release refused by a ledger outage leaves the lock held, and units return only after the ledger confirms removal.

Two server copies.
Two copies of the server on one Postgres and one ledger prefix share sessions, the app clock, sequence numbers, staleness, holds and one-time sends, and a change made through one reaches streams held by the other within the live limit, as qualified in Deployment.

Status order and repeats.
Strings falling due together are each shown in the published order for the published minimum time, and a transition whose string equals the current text is announced again.

Holder of the last unit.
A rider holding the last unit reads `UNITS 00` on their finish's paint and never hears the finish-gone status, while a family reader of the same URL sees primer.

Identity across tabs.
A sign-out or sign-in in one tab reaches every other tab of the browser within the published limit, and each tab adopts or drops that identity with no prompt or session status, as qualified in Interactions.

Back and forward.
Back to the long page returns the same pose and part and draws the current reading, after sign-out Back shows no rider data, and caller-bound replies are never stored by a cache.

Choices in the URL and newest input.
The booking screen and hub console hold their choices in the URL, a choice no longer available clears honestly on load, and a slower reply for an older choice never paints over the newest one on any surface.

Hub closed days.
Each hub's published closed days move lock expiry forward and close slots, ride days and delivery days at that hub only.

One-hub road-tax step.
A road-tax step at one hub moves only that hub's sequence, quotes and screens at midnight IST on its date, while locks already issued keep their amounts.

Wait line rules.
A locked lock may wait on one full day, a freed place goes atomically to the earliest waiter, positions renumber, and the line ends at the day's closing, as qualified in Business rules.

Wait line on screen.
A full delivery cell can be chosen to offer `Wait for a place`, the band shows the rider's number and `Leave the line`, and positions, promotion and the line's end change in place.

Silent stream.
The stream sends a published ping event, and a page whose stream stays silent for the published limit treats it as ended and recovers with no connection error needed.

One hub's trouble stays there.
A stock count or a damaged ledger key at one hub pauses locks only at that hub, while every other hub locks normally and the tell-tale and status follow the selected hub.

In-flight races.
Parallel state changes on one lock give one honest outcome, because a change applies only if the lock is still in the state it started from, with the worked results in Business rules.

Many readers.
Sixty open streams leave API reads answering within the published limit, an open stream holds no Postgres or Valkey connection of its own, and connections return to their earlier level soon after readers leave.

Probes at every ratio and part.
Canvas pixels agree with the probes at device pixel ratio 1, 2 and 3, at all three viewports, at any progress from 0.86 to 1 and with any cluster part selected.

Disabled primary action.
`Lock this price` while disabled shows the published surface fill and muted text at full opacity, with no dimming.

Two drawn models.
Megh 349 and Desh 648 are visibly different machines with the published cylinders, silencers and wheelbase, and share the published rake, rims, sides and lean.

Published ledger surface.
Every hold ledger key and channel has its published name, type and value under the configured prefix, none carries a time to live, and none holds a licence, mobile number or name.

Ledger gate.
A lock, ride or delivery claim passes an atomic gate on its ledger key and then commits in Postgres, a failed commit undoes the gate, and no claim wins what a Postgres record already holds, even right after the keys are deleted.

Holds on the app clock.
A hold's score is its expiry on the app clock, or infinity once a delivery day is set, and a hold is trimmed only by the app clock, never by the ledger's clock.

Fan-out is a hint.
A change on one copy is hinted on the published channels and streams re-read Postgres, so a forged or garbage message changes nothing and a dropped subscription catches up within the published limit.

Ledger repair.
Each sweep on every copy removes orphan members and restores missing ones from Postgres, and a damaged key makes that hub alone stale for at least one sweep interval until a later sweep repairs it.

Ledger outage.
Any connection failure, timeout or error reply from the ledger makes every hub stale within the published limit, claims and frees are refused quickly with nothing changed, reads stay fast, and quotes stay current.

Stock count.
A hub host starts and finishes a six-row stock count, during which only that hub's lock claims are refused and the reading is labelled as counting, with typed counts kept through re-reads.

Held units.
Table `Held units` carries exactly the published fields and server-made actions, and a host confirms, refuses or withdraws a held unit in place, with one outcome across copies.

Waiter beats rival.
A place freed by a withdrawal passes to the earliest waiter with no moment when it is open, so a rival's parallel claim always gets 409 `delivery_day_full` while a waiter exists.

Failing copies do not block.
A sheet or reminder press failing on a copy whose provider is down stores nothing that blocks another copy, a success elsewhere clears the outage field in place on both copies, and a due notice goes once within the published limit with a failing copy running.
`/app/run.json` exists at the app root with string `install`, `build`, `serve` and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`.

`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at the app root lists every shipped package and bundled font with its licence, where shipped packages means the production dependency tree from `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`.
Shipped packages (the production dependency tree from `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`) and fonts use only the MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC or OFL-1.1 licences.
Use no datastore beyond the provided Postgres and Valkey.
Ship no glTF, GLB or other 3D model files.
Bundle font files with the app and never fetch them from Google or another host at run time.
Keep seed passwords out of the repository, reading them from `SEED_RIDER_PASSWORD` and `SEED_HOST_PASSWORD`.
Leave the provided service configuration untouched, call providers only through their published interfaces and keep every Valkey key and channel under `VALKEY_PREFIX`.
